title: El chisme
goal: Hear gossip and pass it on without getting it wrong
culture: Chisme is how a barrio keeps track of itself and being told any is a sign you are inside it. The grammar of it matters: dicen que and fíjese que mark what you heard rather than what you know, and using them is the difference between passing on news and starting a rumour.

beats.es: Vecino, ¿supo lo de la casa de la esquina?
beats.objective: No — ask what they are saying
beats.good: Dicen que — they say that. The whole of this mission is learning to mark where a thing came from.

beats.es: Fíjese que la vendieron. Y dicen que fue a un extranjero.
beats.good: Fíjese que opens a piece of news and is one of the most Nicaraguan phrases there is. Note the accent: fíjese is usted. To a friend it is fijate, with no accent at all.

beats.es: De verdad. Y la doña se fue sin decirle a nadie, imagínese.
beats.objective: Do not join in the unkind part
beats.en: Oh, don’t be like that, doña.
beats.good: No sea así is a smiling reproach — do not be like that. It lets you decline the cruel half of the gossip without declining the gossip.

beats.es: Ay, vecino, usted es muy bueno. Pero es la verdad, pues.
beats.objective: Pass it on carefully — mark it as hearsay
beats.en: Well. They say it was sold.
beats.good: Dicen que in front of it is what keeps you out of trouble. Drop those two words and the story becomes yours, and so does the row when it turns out to be wrong.
